sections.bio:
Priya has led controls teams in food, pharma and automotive plants for sixteen years. She founded Northwind after one too many weekends rewriting ladder logic that a line lead could have described in a sentence.

She speaks about safety-rated generated code at industry events and still commissions one line a year herself.

sections.title: Pay per line, cancel any month

items.title: Does Northwind replace our PLCs?
items.body: No. It sits beside them and generates the logic they run, so your hardware and safety certification stay in place.

items.title: How long does commissioning take?
items.body: Most single lines are live within two weeks, including factory acceptance testing.

items.title: Can line operators change recipes?
items.body: Yes, within limits an engineer sets. Every change is logged with who, when and what.

items.title: Where is our data stored?
items.body: In the EU by default, on-premise with the Enterprise tier.

sections.title: Frequently asked questions
sections.lede: Grouped by who usually asks.

items.title: Which controllers are supported?
items.body: Siemens S7-1200/1500, Rockwell ControlLogix and CompactLogix, Beckhoff TwinCAT 3.

items.title: Can we edit the generated code?
items.body: You can, but changes to the description are the supported path; edited blocks are flagged in the audit trail.

items.title: What does a rollout cost?
items.body: Starter is €490 per line per month; a plant programme is quoted per site.

items.title: Do you train line leads?
items.body: Yes. A half-day session on site is part of every commissioning.

What you bring

  • Five years with Siemens or Rockwell controllers
  • One commissioning you are proud of and one you are not

sections.html:
Why we moved sensor logic to the edge

For six years every sensor on a Northwind line reported to the PLC and nowhere else. That was simple and it was slow. Last spring we moved the first layer of logic to the sensor gateway.

Latency

A light curtain trip now stops the station in four milliseconds instead of forty. Nobody noticed the forty; everybody noticed the four.

Resilience

When the PLC reboots, the gateway keeps the interlocks. The line does not restart on its own, but it does not do anything surprising either.

The best control code is the code nobody has to read.

What changes for you

Nothing in the description. The generator decides what runs where.
